data.reason: WAN NIC vtnet0 transmit path is hung: repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flaps in dmesg, 48211 Oerrs on vtnet0, and sendto failing with ENOBUFS ("No buffer space available") even to the directly-connected ISP gateway 198.51.100.1, while the lease is valid, the default route is present, the LAN works, and the modem reports OPERATIONAL. The watchdog already performed 4 interface reloads during this outage (12 in 24h, cap reached) with rc=0 but no recovery, so a reload does not reset the stuck queue; only a host reboot will re-init the device.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a stuck transmit queue (repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" and link DOWN/UP flaps), so no packets can leave toward the ISP even though the interface is up, its lease is valid and the route/modem are fine.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" alternating with "vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP", i.e. the driver keeps timing out on the same TX queue.

ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (the directly-connected ISP gateway) fails with "ping: sendto: No buffer space available", 100% loss - the failure is at the WAN NIC output path, not beyond the provider; same for 1.1.1.1.
netstat -i shows vtnet0 with 48211 Oerrs while Ierrs/Idrop are 0 - errors only on transmit.
ifconfig vtnet0 still reports status active at 10Gbase-T and inet 198.51.100.27; netstat -rn still has default via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0, so addressing/routing are intact.
/var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 holds a valid lease (fixed-address 198.51.100.27, renew 2026/3/5), so the outage is not an expired or lost DHCP lease.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: reloads_in_outage 4, last_action "reload"; events.jsonl logs reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55 and 03:25 all rc=0 with no recovery, then at 03:30 action "none", reason "reload_cap" (reloads_24h 12 of max 12) - interface reloads cannot clear the stuck queue.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl: modem logged "No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out" at 02:01:44 then "Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete" at 02:28:21 and cm_status OPERATIONAL since, so the provider side has recovered while gw.lan still cannot send.
Local path is healthy: mon.lan pings 10.20.0.1 with 0% loss (0.38 ms) while the internet stays down, matching "local services still work".
uptime shows 41 days 23:02 without a reset, consistent with a long-lived driver/NIC hang that only a device re-initialisation clears.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall to re-initialize the hung vtnet0 device (already requested; the harness ran it once). Verify afterwards that the WAN pings the ISP gateway and that dmesg stops logging new "vtnet0: watchdog timeout" lines. If the timeouts return after the reboot, treat the VirtIO WAN NIC/driver as faulty or outdated: update the driver/virtio stack or replace the interface, and have the wan-watchdog escalate to a host reboot instead of repeated interface reloads when reloads stop restoring traffic (the 12-per-24h cap was reached during this outage). Separately, ask the ISP about the 02:01 T3 ranging timeout / unrequested modem reboot and the high uncorrected codeword count (152, worst channel 615 MHz), which started the episode.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN transmit queue hung (watchdog timeouts)
